# Results — Study 385 (Jobless-Claims-Momentum)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The macro-nowcasting
folklore — **rising initial jobless claims call equity downturns early** — tested on the
monthly **4-week-MA initial-claims** tape (a hardcoded, never-revised snapshot of FRED
`IC4WSA`, since FRED's CSV endpoint is firewalled in this build) against month-end **SPY**
(yfinance, total-return adjusted). We split forward 1/3/6/12-month SPY returns into months
when claims momentum is **rising** vs **falling**, compare each to the unconditional base
rate, and add a Welch *t*, a placebo null, a lead/lag scan and a tradable timing overlay.
Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Claims tape | FRED `IC4WSA` — initial claims, SA, 4-week MA (thousands); **hardcoded monthly snapshot**, never-revised |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted), month-end sampled |
| Window | 1993-01-31 → 2026-06-30 (**402** months; **33.4** years) |
| Signal | claims momentum = 4-wk-MA level vs **3 months** prior; **RISING** when > 0 |
| Entry / costs | **1-month execution lag** (act on the next month-end close); 10 bps one-way per switch on the overlay |

> **Snapshot caveat (named on the Signal axis).** FRED is firewalled here, so the claims
> series is a hardcoded monthly snapshot of the 4-week MA — public, well-known, and frozen,
> but **not the real-time vintage** (initial claims are revised, and our table uses the
> settled print). The famous **COVID-2020 spike** (the 4-wk MA peaked near **4,170k** in
> April 2020) is included faithfully and, being one enormous coincident shock, dominates any
> claims-vs-returns association — a fact the verdict leans on, not around.

## The signal — forward SPY returns when claims are RISING vs the base rate

1-month execution lag; the base column is *all* months. The believers say RISING claims
should depress the forward return; Welch *t* compares the RISING-set mean to the
unconditional mean (a real early-warning ⇒ **significantly negative** *t*). The placebo *p*
is the share of 20,000 random same-size month draws whose mean forward return is **at most**
the RISING set's (i.e. as bearish or more).

| horizon | n rising | rising mean | falling mean | base mean | rising down-rate | base down-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 174 | **+0.69%** | +1.15% | +0.95% | 36% | 35% | **−0.63** | 0.201 |
| 3-month  | 172 | **+2.30%** | +3.30% | +2.87% | 31% | 28% | **−0.76** | 0.149 |
| 6-month  | 171 | **+4.91%** | +6.49% | +5.80% | 29% | 24% | **−0.81** | 0.137 |
| 12-month | 168 | **+10.38%** | +13.29% | +12.04% | 24% | 18% | **−0.94** | 0.098 |

Read it carefully. The **direction matches the folklore** at every horizon: when claims are
rising, forward SPY returns are **lower** than the base rate (e.g. **+10.4% vs +12.0%** at 12
months) and the down-rate is higher (**24% vs 18%**). But the gap is small and **never
clears the significance bar** — the most negative Welch *t* is **−0.94** (12-month), with a
placebo *p* of **0.10**. A real but statistically unproven tilt: the right sign, inside the
noise.

## The decisive test — does the claims uptick *lead* the market?

The whole pitch is **"early."** So we scan the correlation of claims momentum at *t* against
the SPY return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. A genuine early-warning would show its strongest
*negative* correlation at a **positive** lead (claims move first, the market falls later).

| lead *L* (months) | −3 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +3 | +6 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(claims-mom, fwd SPY) | **−0.19** | +0.10 | +0.05 | +0.05 | +0.03 | +0.11 |

The strongest negative correlation sits at **L = −3** — claims momentum is most associated
with the market move *three months in its **past***. At positive leads (claims supposedly
leading) the correlation is near **zero or positive**. Claims aren't an early-warning; the
uptick is a **coincident-to-lagging** echo of a market that already turned. That is the
core of the "early-warning? — Not supported" stamp.

## Tradability — the "go to cash when claims are rising" overlay

Hold SPY when claims are falling, sit in cash when rising (one-month lag; 10 bps per switch,
turnover one-way × NAV). Sharpe is excess-of-zero (the cash leg earns 0 here — a
conservative, labelled simplification).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | switches |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold SPY | **+11.4%** | **0.77** | — |
| overlay, gross | +7.3% | 0.75 | 109 |
| overlay, net @ 10 bps | **+7.0%** | **0.72** | 109 |

The overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold** on both return (**+7.0% vs +11.4%** net) and
Sharpe (**0.72 vs 0.77**). Sitting out the market whenever claims tick up forfeits return
without buying enough downside protection to pay for it — even *before* costs. The signal
isn't merely un-extractable; acting on it **loses money relative to doing nothing.**

## Robustness — window, threshold, and the COVID dependence

| variation | n rising | rising 12m mean | base 12m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| momentum **k = 1** | 167 | +10.53% | +12.04% | −0.90 | 0.120 |
| momentum **k = 3** (base) | 168 | +10.38% | +12.04% | **−0.94** | 0.098 |
| momentum **k = 6** | 136 | +8.49% | +12.04% | **−1.74** | 0.008 |
| threshold **> +10%** | 32 | +16.20% | +12.04% | **+1.02** | 0.927 |
| **drop 2020–2021** (ex-COVID), 12m | 162 | +10.35% | +12.88% | −1.32 | 0.033 |

Two lessons. (1) The effect *strengthens with a slower window* (k = 6 → *t* = −1.74) — but a
6-month-old claims trend is the opposite of an **early** warning. (2) Push the threshold to a
**big** claims jump (> +10%) and the sign **flips positive** (*t* = +1.02): the largest
upticks are recession *bottoms* you'd want to be buying, not selling. And dropping the COVID
years leaves the 12-month *t* at **−1.32** — still under the bar. No specification clears
*t* = 2 at the canonical "early" (k ≤ 3) horizon.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly claims + SPY-like series with a *planted* link (rising claims
momentum at *t* depresses the *t+1* return by `edge`). The detector + inference must recover
a planted edge and must **not** manufacture significance when the true edge is zero.

| planted edge (monthly) | n rising | rising 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 172 | +0.61% | +0.74% | **−0.36** | 0.338 |
| **+0.04** (large link) | 172 | −2.88% | −1.23% | **−4.40** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted link the test sits at *t* = −0.36 (no false positive); a large planted
link drives *t* to **−4.40**. The machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape *t* of ~−0.9 is
exactly what an *absent-or-tiny* claims→returns edge looks like through this keyhole.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The folklore's **direction is real** — rising claims precede modestly
  lower, more often-negative forward returns at every horizon — but the excess **fails the
  *t* ≥ 2 bar** (best Welch *t* = −0.94, placebo *p* = 0.10), is fragile to the momentum
  window, **flips sign** for the biggest upticks, and softens further ex-COVID. A real-as-
  lore, weak-as-edge tilt, not a certified signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "cash when claims rise" overlay **underperforms
  buy-and-hold** gross *and* net (**+7.0% vs +11.4%**, Sharpe **0.72 vs 0.77**). The signal
  doesn't just fail to add value — acting on it **destroys** return. Nothing to allocate to.
- **Early warning? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The lead/lag scan puts the strongest negative
  correlation at **L = −3** (claims momentum *lagging* the market by a quarter); at positive
  leads it's ~zero. Claims are a **coincident-to-lagging** echo, not a leader. The whole
  appeal — *early* — is the part the data rejects.
